key_takeaways: unknown keeps a value checked until you narrow it; any removes checking from everything derived from it.
Assertions are unchecked promises; keep them rare, commented and backed by evidence.
never in a default branch turns a missing union case into a compile error.

exercise.title: Move one boundary from any to unknown
exercise.instructions: Change a function that accepts outside data to take unknown, add a narrowing or schema step that yields the domain type, document each remaining assertion with its evidence, and add an exhaustive default to one switch over a union. Record compiler output before and after.
exercise.deliverable: A diff that replaces an any boundary with unknown plus narrowing, a list of remaining assertions with evidence, and compiler output before and after.
hints: A type predicate (value is User) lets one runtime check narrow at every call site.
Search for 'as any' and '!' first; each is a place checking stopped on purpose or by accident.
The default branch of an exhaustive switch should assign to a never-typed variable.

questions.prompt: Which type should a function use for a `fetch` response body it has just parsed with `JSON.parse`?
choices: any, because the shape is not known yet
unknown, so nothing can be used until it is narrowed
object, because JSON is always an object
never, because the value is untrusted
questions.correct_answer: unknown, so nothing can be used until it is narrowed
questions.explanation: unknown keeps the value checked; narrowing or a schema check produces the domain type.

questions.prompt: `const n: number = (payload as any).id` compiles although `id` is a string at runtime. Why?
choices: Numbers and strings are compatible in TypeScript
any disables checking on the value and everything derived from it
questions.correct_answer: any disables checking on the value and everything derived from it
questions.explanation: Property access on any yields any, which is assignable to number without a check.

questions.prompt: What does assigning the switch subject to a `never`-typed variable in the `default` branch achieve?
choices: It throws at runtime for unknown cases
It makes a newly added union member a compile error until handled
It converts the union to a string
questions.correct_answer: It makes a newly added union member a compile error until handled
questions.explanation: After all members are narrowed away the subject is never; a new member breaks that assignment.

questions.prompt: A teammate writes `const user = data as User` after parsing JSON and says the compiler now guarantees the shape. Correct the claim.
questions.correct_answer: An assertion is an unchecked promise: it tells the compiler to treat the value as User without any runtime evidence, so a wrong payload still crashes later. Type data as unknown and narrow it with a type predicate or schema check that actually inspects the fields; keep assertions only where you hold evidence the compiler cannot see, and comment them.
questions.explanation: Assertions bypass checking; narrowing proves the shape.

questions.prompt: Explain why a `typeof value === 'string'` check inside one function does not narrow `value` inside a callback passed to another function.
questions.correct_answer: Narrowing is control-flow analysis within a function body. A callback is a separate function whose parameter type comes from its own declaration, and the compiler cannot know when the callback runs relative to the check, so the narrowed type does not carry across the function boundary. Pass the narrowed value as a typed argument or narrow again inside the callback.
questions.explanation: Control-flow narrowing stops at function boundaries.
questions.learning_objective: Recognize the limits of control-flow narrowing
